The invention provides a viscoelastic composition for improving the operability of an endoscope. In particular, the composition is useful when an opaque or dark-colored liquid is present inside a canal and obstructs the endoscopic field of view. By securing visibility at the distal end of the endoscope, the composition enables an operator to perform observation, diagnosis, or treatment more reliably and efficiently.

The viscoelastic composition functions by being introduced into the canal through the endoscope and pushing aside the liquid that obstructs visibility. Because the composition has suitable viscoelastic properties, it can maintain a space or visual field in front of the endoscope without immediately dispersing or mixing with the surrounding liquid. As a result, the endoscope can obtain a clearer field of view even in an environment where blood, bile, intestinal fluid, or another opaque dark-colored liquid would otherwise interfere with observation.

The viscoelastic composition comprises a substance having viscoelastic properties and water. The viscoelastic substance provides the composition with an appropriate balance of flowability and shape-retaining ability, while the water serves as a medium that allows the composition to be fed through an endoscope channel. This combination makes it possible to deliver the composition smoothly from the proximal side of the endoscope to the distal side while maintaining its ability to displace obstructing liquid at the observation site.

In a preferred embodiment, the viscoelastic composition has a hardness of 550 N/m² or less, a viscosity at 25°C in the range of 200 to 2,000 mPa·s, and a loss tangent of 0.6 or less. These physical properties allow the composition to be readily supplied through the endoscope while also providing sufficient viscoelasticity to secure the field of view. More preferably, the composition has an electrical conductivity of 250 μS/cm or less, which may be advantageous when the endoscope is used together with electrical or high-frequency treatment devices.

The invention also provides a method for securing an endoscopic field of view using the viscoelastic composition. In this method, the composition is fed from a proximal part of the endoscope through a channel extending within the endoscope and discharged from a distal part of the endoscope. Once discharged, the composition moves or pushes aside the opaque liquid present in front of the distal end, thereby forming or maintaining a visible region for endoscopic observation. This method improves endoscope operability and supports safer and more accurate procedures in canals where visibility is compromised by obstructing liquid.

A viscoelastic composition and a method for delivering that composition are provided for improving visibility during endoscopic observation inside a canal or cavity. During an endoscopic procedure, the field of view may be obstructed by an opaque dark liquid, such as blood, bile, intestinal fluid, or another turbid body fluid. Instead of relying only on repeated washing or suction, a water-containing viscoelastic substance is supplied through a channel of the endoscope and discharged from the distal end of the instrument. When introduced into the canal, the viscoelastic substance forms a localized mass or layer that physically displaces the opaque liquid from the observation area, thereby securing a clearer field of view for the endoscope.

The composition is designed to have mechanical and flow properties that allow it to be delivered smoothly while remaining sufficiently cohesive after discharge. In particular, the viscoelastic substance has a low hardness, so that it does not damage or excessively press against tissue in the canal. It also has a controlled viscosity that permits feeding through the endoscope channel without requiring excessive force, while still being viscous enough to remain in the desired region and push aside the surrounding dark liquid. In addition, the composition has a low loss tangent, meaning that it exhibits an elastic character sufficient to maintain its shape and resist immediate mixing or dispersion in the liquid environment. This balance of softness, viscosity, and elasticity gives the material excellent operability during use.

In preferred embodiments, the composition also has low electrical conductivity. This property is advantageous when the endoscopic procedure involves electrosurgical treatment or other electrically operated instruments, because it can reduce undesirable conduction of electrical current through the introduced material. As a result, the composition can be used more safely and effectively in combination with various endoscopic tools.

By feeding the water-containing viscoelastic substance through the endoscope channel and placing it near the distal end of the endoscope, the operator can create a temporary transparent or clearer region in front of the observation window. The material displaces opaque liquid without the need for complete removal of fluid from the canal, allowing the target site to be viewed more reliably. Accordingly, the proposed composition and delivery method improve endoscopic visualization, enhance procedural control, and support safer and more efficient diagnosis or treatment in environments where the field of view would otherwise be obscured.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called a definite article, and it helps us talk about something specific. For example, when we say “a book,” we could mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we are talking about a particular book that the speaker and listener know about.

Although “the” may seem simple, it gives clarity and precision to sentences. It helps identify people, places, objects, and ideas. We use it in everyday phrases such as “the sun,” “the world,” “the best choice,” and “the beginning.” Without this small word, many sentences would sound incomplete or unclear.

In writing, “the” often guides the reader’s attention. It points to something important and makes the meaning more exact. This shows that even the smallest words can have a big impact. “The” may be short, but it is essential to the structure and meaning of English.

counterfactuals.output:
**Purpose of the Invention**

The purpose of the invention is to provide a medical device and associated method for improving visualization during endoscopic procedures by temporarily displacing obstructing liquids, fluids, mucus, blood, irrigation media, or other liquid-phase material from the field of view. More particularly, the invention employs a water-based viscoelastic material that is deliverable through or in association with an endoscope and that, upon deployment, forms a coherent, optically transmissive or substantially clear mass capable of pushing aside surrounding liquid without rapidly dispersing therein. By maintaining a localized viewing window in front of the endoscope, the invention facilitates examination, diagnosis, navigation, and therapeutic intervention in fluid-containing anatomical spaces while reducing the need for repeated suction, irrigation, or instrument repositioning.

**Summary of the Invention**

In one aspect, the invention relates to an endoscopic visualization aid comprising a water-based viscoelastic material configured for introduction into a body lumen, cavity, or other anatomical region during an endoscopic procedure. The viscoelastic material has sufficient cohesiveness, viscosity, and elasticity to remain at least temporarily localized after delivery and to mechanically displace obstructing liquid away from an optical path of an endoscope. The material may be delivered through a working channel of the endoscope, through a dedicated catheter, nozzle, sheath, or other delivery member, and may be positioned adjacent to or in front of an imaging element to create a clear or substantially unobstructed visualization zone. In certain embodiments, the material is biocompatible, water-based, optically transparent or translucent, and removable or dispersible by suction, irrigation, dilution, enzymatic degradation, or natural clearance. The invention also encompasses methods of using the material during endoscopy, including delivering an effective amount of the viscoelastic material to a target site, allowing the material to push aside or separate obstructing liquid from the viewing field, visualizing tissue or instruments through or around the displaced liquid zone, and subsequently removing or permitting clearance of the material after completion of the diagnostic or therapeutic procedure.

**Title:** Viscoelastic Composition and Delivery System for Maintaining Endoscopic Visibility

**Abstract**

An endoscopic visibility maintenance system is disclosed. The system includes an elongate endoscope having a proximal end, a distal end, and at least one working or auxiliary channel extending therebetween, and a viscoelastic composition configured to be fed through the channel from the proximal end toward the distal end. The viscoelastic composition is formulated to adhere temporarily to an observation window, lens cover, transparent cap, or distal viewing surface of the endoscope and to displace blood, mucus, bubbles, tissue debris, and other obscuring matter while permitting optical observation through the composition. In certain embodiments, the composition has a hardness, viscosity at 25°C, loss tangent, and electrical conductivity selected to provide retention at the distal end without preventing delivery through the endoscope channel.

---

## Patent-Style Description

### Field of the Invention

The present invention relates generally to endoscopic instruments and methods, and more particularly to compositions, systems, and methods for maintaining or restoring visibility at a distal end of an endoscope during observation, diagnosis, or treatment inside a body cavity, lumen, organ, or surgical field.

### Background

During endoscopic procedures, the visual field at the distal end of an endoscope may be degraded by blood, mucus, bile, lavage fluid, tissue fragments, bubbles, fat, smoke residue, or other contaminants. Conventional irrigation and suction techniques can temporarily clear the field, but the distal optical surface may quickly become re-obscured. Gas insufflation or liquid flushing may also disturb the operative field, impair visualization, or require repeated manipulation.

There remains a need for a material that can be delivered from a proximal portion of an endoscope to a distal portion and that can maintain a transparent or substantially transparent viewing region at or near the distal optical surface.

### Summary of the Invention

In one aspect, an invention provides a viscoelastic composition for maintaining visibility at a distal end of an endoscope. The viscoelastic composition is configured to be introduced into a proximal port of the endoscope and advanced through an internal channel to a distal discharge opening, where the composition forms a coherent, transparent or translucent mass, layer, plug, bead, film, or meniscus adjacent to a distal viewing surface.

In certain embodiments, the viscoelastic composition has:

- a hardness of about **5 to about 80 Shore 00**, or about **10 to about 60 Shore 00**;
- a viscosity at **25°C** of about **1,000 mPa·s to about 1,000,000 mPa·s**, preferably about **5,000 mPa·s to about 300,000 mPa·s**, as measured at a shear rate suitable for endoscopic injection;
- a loss tangent, tan δ, of about **0.05 to about 1.5**, preferably about **0.1 to about 0.8**, at 25°C and 1 Hz;
- an electrical conductivity of about **0.001 S/m to about 2.0 S/m**, preferably about **0.01 S/m to about 1.5 S/m**; and
- optical clarity sufficient to permit observation through at least a portion of the composition when disposed adjacent to an endoscopic imaging window.

In another aspect, a system is provided comprising an endoscope and a delivery device containing the viscoelastic composition. The delivery device may include a syringe, cartridge, pump, pressurized reservoir, screw-driven injector, peristaltic pump, or motorized dispensing unit coupled to a proximal port of the endoscope.

In another aspect, a method is provided for maintaining endoscopic visibility. The method includes providing an endoscope having a proximal end, a distal end, an imaging element at or near the distal end, and a channel extending from the proximal end to the distal end; introducing a viscoelastic composition into the channel at the proximal end; feeding the viscoelastic composition through the channel toward the distal end; discharging the composition from an opening at or near the distal end; and positioning the composition adjacent to the imaging element so as to displace or exclude obscuring material from a field of view.

### Detailed Description

In embodiments of the invention, the viscoelastic composition is selected to exhibit both flowability and retention. The composition is sufficiently deformable to pass through an endoscope channel under manual or mechanical pressure, but sufficiently elastic or cohesive to remain at the distal end after discharge. The composition may form a dome, coating, lens-like layer, transparent plug, or protective interface over a distal optical window.

The composition may be aqueous, non-aqueous, hydrogel-based, silicone-based, glycerol-based, polymer-based, or a combination thereof. Suitable polymers may include, without limitation, polyvinyl alcohol, polyvinylpyrrolidone, polyethylene glycol, polypropylene glycol, hyaluronic acid or salts thereof, cellulose derivatives, alginate, gelatin, polyacrylamide, polyacrylic acid derivatives, polysaccharides, silicone elastomers, urethane gels, and copolymers or mixtures thereof.

The composition may include one or more additives, including saline, buffers, humectants, osmotic agents, surfactants, thickeners, crosslinking agents, radiopaque agents, colorants, antimicrobial agents, lubricants, ionic salts, and electrically conductive components. In certain embodiments, the electrical conductivity is adjusted using physiologically acceptable salts such as sodium chloride, potassium chloride, phosphate salts, or bicarbonate salts.

The viscoelastic composition may be transparent, substantially transparent, or optically transmissive over visible wavelengths. In one embodiment, a layer of the composition having a thickness of 1 mm exhibits at least 60%, at least 70%, at least 80%, or at least 90% transmission of visible light.

### Mechanical and Rheological Properties

The hardness of the composition may be selected to prevent fragmentation while allowing atraumatic contact with tissue. In certain embodiments, the composition has a Shore 00 hardness of about 5 to about 80. In other embodiments, the composition has a Shore 00 hardness of about 10 to about 40.

The viscosity at 25°C may be shear-dependent. In some embodiments, the composition is shear-thinning, such that the composition has a relatively high viscosity at rest and a lower apparent viscosity during injection. The viscosity at 25°C may be about 1,000 mPa·s to about 1,000,000 mPa·s. In certain embodiments, the viscosity is measured using a rotational rheometer at 25°C and at a shear rate of 1 s⁻¹, 10 s⁻¹, or 100 s⁻¹.

The loss tangent, tan δ, may be selected to provide a balance between elastic retention and viscous flow. In certain embodiments, tan δ is less than 1, indicating a predominantly elastic response. In other embodiments, tan δ is between about 0.1 and about 0.8 at 25°C and 1 Hz.

The electrical conductivity may be selected to be compatible with endoscopic visualization, sensing, or electrosurgical environments. In embodiments in which electrosurgical tools are used, the composition may have controlled conductivity to avoid unintended insulation or uncontrolled current concentration. The electrical conductivity may be about 0.001 S/m to about 2.0 S/m at 25°C.

### Delivery from Proximal End to Distal End

The viscoelastic composition may be stored in a container coupled to a proximal portion of the endoscope. The container may be connected to a working channel, irrigation channel, auxiliary channel, or dedicated visibility-maintenance channel. The composition may be fed by applying pressure at the proximal end, for example by depressing a syringe plunger, actuating a pump, compressing a reservoir, or rotating a screw-driven dispensing mechanism.

In one method, the distal end of the endoscope is positioned near a target site. When visibility is impaired or before visibility is impaired, a predetermined amount of the viscoelastic composition is introduced into the proximal port. The composition is advanced through the channel and discharged from a distal opening located adjacent to the imaging window. The composition then contacts or covers at least part of the distal viewing surface and forms a protective layer that resists washout by bodily fluids.

The amount delivered may be about 0.01 mL to about 10 mL, depending on the endoscope size and procedure. In some embodiments, the delivered amount is about 0.05 mL to about 2 mL. The composition may be delivered intermittently, continuously, or in pulses.

The distal discharge opening may be oriented toward the optical window, toward a transparent distal cap, or toward the forward field of view. In some embodiments, the channel terminates in an annular or circumferential outlet arranged around the imaging window, thereby forming a uniform layer or meniscus over the field of view. In other embodiments, a nozzle or deflector directs the composition across the imaging surface.

### Exemplary Method

A method for maintaining endoscopic visibility may comprise:

1. providing an endoscope having a proximal end, a distal end, an imaging window at the distal end, and a lumen extending from the proximal end to the distal end;
2. providing a viscoelastic composition having a Shore 00 hardness of about 5 to about 80, a viscosity at 25°C of about 1,000 to about 1,000,000 mPa·s, a loss tangent of about 0.05 to about 1.5, and an electrical conductivity of about 0.001 to about 2.0 S/m;
3. coupling a reservoir containing the viscoelastic composition to a proximal port of the endoscope;
4. applying pressure to the reservoir to feed the composition through the lumen from the proximal end toward the distal end;
5. discharging the composition from a distal outlet at or near the imaging window; and
6. maintaining a coherent quantity of the composition adjacent to the imaging window so that blood, mucus, bubbles, fluid, or debris is displaced from the optical path.

### Representative Claims

1. **An endoscopic visibility maintenance system**, comprising:  
   an endoscope having a proximal end, a distal end, an imaging element disposed at or near the distal end, and a channel extending from the proximal end toward the distal end; and  
   a viscoelastic composition configured to be fed through the channel and discharged at the distal end,  
   wherein the viscoelastic composition has a Shore 00 hardness of about 5 to about 80, a viscosity at 25°C of about 1,000 mPa·s to about 1,000,000 mPa·s, a loss tangent of about 0.05 to about 1.5, and an electrical conductivity of about 0.001 S/m to about 2.0 S/m.

2. **The system of claim 1**, wherein the viscoelastic composition is substantially transparent and is configured to form an optically transmissive layer adjacent to an imaging window of the endoscope.

3. **The system of claim 1**, wherein the channel is a working channel, an irrigation channel, or a dedicated delivery channel.

4. **The system of claim 1**, further comprising a syringe, pump, cartridge, or pressurized reservoir coupled to a proximal port of the endoscope and configured to advance the viscoelastic composition through the channel.

5. **The system of claim 1**, wherein the viscoelastic composition comprises a hydrogel including at least one polymer selected from hyaluronic acid, polyvinyl alcohol, polyvinylpyrrolidone, polyethylene glycol, cellulose derivatives, alginate, gelatin, and combinations thereof.

6. **A method of maintaining endoscopic visibility**, comprising:  
   introducing a viscoelastic composition into a proximal port of an endoscope;  
   feeding the viscoelastic composition through a channel extending from a proximal end of the endoscope to a distal end of the endoscope;  
   discharging the viscoelastic composition from a distal outlet; and  
   positioning the viscoelastic composition adjacent to an imaging window at the distal end,  
   wherein the viscoelastic composition displaces obscuring material from a field of view and has a viscosity at 25°C of about 1,000 mPa·s to about 1,000,000 mPa·s.

7. **The method of claim 6**, wherein the viscoelastic composition has a loss tangent of about 0.1 to about 0.8 and remains as a coherent optically transmissive mass adjacent to the imaging window during observation.

8. **The method of claim 6**, wherein feeding the viscoelastic composition comprises applying pressure to a syringe or actuating a pump coupled to the proximal port.

9. **The method of claim 6**, wherein the viscoelastic composition has an electrical conductivity of about 0.01 S/m to about 1.5 S/m.

10. **The method of claim 6**, further comprising intermittently delivering additional viscoelastic composition from the proximal end to the distal end during an endoscopic procedure to restore visibility after partial displacement of a previously delivered quantity.

A viscoelastic aqueous composition and method are provided for clearing an endoscope field of view when opaque dark liquid, such as blood or bile, accumulates at an observation site. The composition comprises water and a biocompatible viscoelastic agent in an amount effective to form a coherent, optically transmissive bolus or stream having sufficient viscosity and elasticity to displace the opaque liquid without rapidly mixing with it. Optional components include salts, buffers, surfactants, contrast agents, preservatives, or coloring agents compatible with endoscopic use.

In use, the composition is delivered through an instrument or irrigation channel of an endoscope to the distal tip adjacent the imaging window. Upon discharge, the viscoelastic aqueous composition pushes, separates, or blankets the opaque dark liquid, creating a temporary clear optical path between the endoscope and target tissue. The composition may be applied intermittently or continuously during diagnostic or therapeutic endoscopy, allowing visualization and procedure continuation without removing the endoscope or relying solely on low-viscosity irrigation. The invention is particularly useful in gastrointestinal, bronchoscopic, urologic, and surgical endoscopic procedures where bleeding or other dark fluid obscures visualization.
